question: Should embedded-surface guidance retain compatibility with released `@openclaw/design-system` v0.1.x, or should it target a newly released/versioned Carapace CSS contract instead?
rationale: The generated downstream content cannot safely choose between legacy compatibility, a version-gated candidate contract, or publishing a matching release; that package-support boundary needs maintainer intent.

options.title: Version-gate the new guidance
options.body: Keep legacy guidance within the released v0.1.x token surface and expose the embedded token mapping only for an explicitly versioned compatible package.

options.title: Release the matching CSS contract
options.body: Publish CSS that defines the documented token set, then regenerate the project skill against that released version.

options.title: Defer embedded guidance
options.body: Remove or postpone the new embedded-surface reference until the package and compatibility contract are settled.

recommendation.title: Version-gate the new guidance
recommendation.body: Keep legacy guidance within the released v0.1.x token surface and expose the embedded token mapping only for an explicitly versioned compatible package.

likelyOwner.reason: They documented the concrete compatibility boundary and the required upstream resolution choices in the PR discussion.
